points.description: States one valid advantage of the observer over a filter, with correct reasoning. Acceptable: uses the known input u and plant model to predict rather than differentiate, so it tracks changing velocity with no/less lag within its bandwidth (a low-pass filter trades lag against smoothing); OR it estimates a state not directly measured, not just a smoothed differentiated signal; OR quantisation enters through a bounded filtered path rather than being divided by T. A bare claim with no reason (e.g. 'it is better' or 'more accurate') earns nothing.

States one valid circumstance where the filter is safer, specifically invoking model error or parameter uncertainty. Acceptable: the filter is model-free, whereas the observer is biased/misleading when A, B or actuator gain are wrong; OR plant parameters drift (temperature, load, wear) or strong nonlinearity away from the linearisation point; OR a badly identified model/sign error can make the observer diverge. Generic reasons not tied to model error (e.g. 'simpler', 'cheaper to compute') earn nothing.

rubric.notes: Award 1 mark for a valid, reasoned observer advantage and 1 mark for a filter-favouring circumstance that cites model error or parameter uncertainty. Marks are whole only. Vague statements without reasoning, or filter reasons unrelated to model uncertainty, earn no mark.
